claim: James Brady is an engineer at Elicit
source_quote: James Brady, engineer at Elicit, delivered a talk on making AI agent workflows trustworthy and verifiable

claim: Ashpl is named after the Old English diphthong 'ash' Æ combined with PL
source_quote: These three principles led Elicit to build Ashpl (named after the Old English diphthong 'ash' Æ combined with PL)

claim: Ashpl is Turing-incomplete and purely functional
source_quote: Turing-incomplete and purely functional: No loops, no recursion, no mutation. This makes the language predictable and cacheable.

claim: Ashpl is an opinionated subset of Python
source_quote: Opinionated subset of Python: Not a random simplification — they removed unhelpful Python features and added domain-specific primitives (retrieving academic papers, clinical trials, web searches).

claim: Ashpl is typed
source_quote: Typed: Enables fast error detection and cheap redrafts when type errors occur.

claim: Ashpl is reactive
source_quote: Reactive: The system writes, interprets, and rewrites Ashpl in a constant loop.

claim: Content addressing and caching makes full-rewrite approach viable
source_quote: This is described as 'super duper crucial.' Because Ashpl is purely functional with no mutation, the system can hash each expression and memoize results.

claim: Reinterpreting a 1,000-line program from scratch would be prohibitively slow without caching
source_quote: without it, reinterpreting a 1,000-line program from scratch each time would be prohibitively slow

claim: UI communicates with an append-only event log using event sourcing pattern
source_quote: UI communicates with an append-only event log (event sourcing pattern)

claim: Gateway handles API keys and credential isolation to prevent prompt injection attacks
source_quote: Gateway handles API keys and credential isolation — user input never flows directly to the curator, preventing prompt injection attacks

claim: Elicit is currently using Pi with Anthropic models as the best combination
source_quote: Currently using Pi with Anthropic models as the best combination

claim: Elicit has used Anthropic's agent SDK and Pi with Claude/Codex
source_quote: Wrapper layer allows swapping between different model harnesses (they've used Anthropic's agent SDK, and Pi with Claude/Codex)

claim: The demo extended the same program to 1,000+ lines when adding new layers
source_quote: Adding new layers (commercialization strategies, oversight bodies, cross-referencing) extends the same program to 1,000+ lines

claim: Elicit is 'very happy' with the event sourcing pattern
source_quote: Consider event sourcing — Elicit is very happy with this pattern

claim: There are three core requirements for Elicit's research agent: Legibility, Fidelity during iteration, and Faithful execution
source_quote: Elicit's research agent was built around three core requirements: 1. Legibility... 2. Fidelity during iteration... 3. Faithful execution...

claim: Drift during iteration is a common failure mode in agentic systems
source_quote: Fidelity during iteration: When users iterate on results... the system must not drift from the original intent. This is a common failure mode in agentic systems

claim: The key trade-off is speed versus rigor
source_quote: The key trade-off is speed versus rigor: high-quality, defensive work naturally takes longer than surface-level analysis.

claim: Base your DSL on an existing language with lots of training data examples
source_quote: Base your DSL on an existing language with lots of training data examples — the model doesn't need to learn syntax, just the subset

claim: Managing model output streams is 'surprisingly annoying'
source_quote: Manage model output streams — surprisingly annoying to handle properly

claim: Dedicated evaluation for DSL-based systems is critical but extremely complex
source_quote: Invest in dedicated evaluation — critical but extremely complex for DSL-based systems
